title: Mastering the Gap: Full Thickness Macular Hole (FTMH)
summary: A full-thickness macular hole (FTMH) is a definitive anatomical defect in the fovea, extending from the internal limiting membrane to the outer segments of the photoreceptors. This condition results in a significant loss of central vision and requires precise surgical intervention.

sections.title: Defining the Defect
sections.content: A Full Thickness Macular Hole (FTMH) is a primary foveal break that involves all layers of the neurosensory retina. It is most commonly idiopathic and occurs frequently in women over the age of 60. The condition is characterized by the sudden or progressive loss of central vision and the presence of metamorphopsia (distorted vision).

rows: Foveal detachment; loss of foveal depression.
Eccentric or central break in neurosensory retina.
Complete defect; no posterior vitreous detachment (PVD).
FTMH with complete Posterior Vitreous Detachment (PVD).
Full thickness defect; cystic edges; cuff of subretinal fluid.
Partial thickness; intact outer retinal layers; 'scooped out' look.
Steep foveal edges caused by ERM; no loss of tissue.
History of sun gazing; small outer retinal defect.
Petaloid pattern on FA; intraretinal fluid but no break.

sections.title: Diagnostic Bedside Tests
content: Watzke-Allen Test: Patient perceives a break/thinning in a narrow slit beam over the fovea.
Laser Aim Beam Test: 50μm laser spot is not seen when directed into the center of the hole.
Amsler Grid: Central scotoma and significant metamorphopsia.
OCT (Gold Standard): Confirms full-thickness loss, measures hole diameter, and identifies VMT status.

sections.title: Surgical Management Process
content: 1. Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) to remove vitreous traction.
2. Induction of Posterior Vitreous Detachment (if not present).
3. Internal Limiting Membrane (ILM) Peeling to relieve tangential traction.
4. Gas Tamponade (SF6 or C3F8) to seal the hole edges.

sections.title: Critical Post-Op Red Flags
content: Sudden increase in pain or redness (Endophthalmitis)
New onset of 'curtain' or 'shadow' in vision (Retinal Detachment)
Elevated Intraocular Pressure (IOP) due to gas expansion
Progression of Nuclear Sclerotic Cataracts (Commonly post-vitrectomy)

content.explanation: P: Pars Plana Vitrectomy; E: Excision of the ILM; E: Exchange of fluid for gas; L: Low-head positioning (Face-down).
